D13·dvkc — 2026-08-05
chose: Statusline D13, four changes (user request): (a) the task gauge becomes a fixed five-cell ▰▱ track via a new kernel barFor — filled run toned by state (success complete / warn in progress), unfilled remainder dim; (b) the $cost segment is removed entirely; (c) ctx moves ahead of cache; (d) the constant `ctx` label dims to gray and only the number+% carries the band tone. barFor is statusline-scoped — pieFor and its ○◔◑◕● are untouched and still serve sofar next / list. This retires D7's promise that the plain --no-color line stays byte-identical to 0.8.0: dropping cost and reordering are content changes that apply in both modes
over: Keeping the pie and accepting the jitter; switching to the ▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█ block ramp (one cell, 8 steps, but fill height still reads as size change); dropping the gauge entirely and letting 9/10 carry it; and changing pieFor globally so all three surfaces share the new ramp (D9's one-product argument)
because: The pie's ○◔◑◕● members are East-Asian-Ambiguous width, so terminals resolve them to different advance widths — often a different font for the quarter-filled ones — and every segment after the gauge shifted horizontally as progress moved. A status bar re-renders constantly; a gauge that reflows the line is worse than no gauge. Five cells cost four columns and buy total stability. Cost went because the rent-meter's dollar figure stopped being the thing being watched; ctx moved first because it is the segment that governs when to act. Dimming the invariant label is the same word-over-glyph logic as D10/D11 taken one step further: gray what never changes so the eye lands on what does.
